outline.rationale: The user is new to ML and wants to read foundational RLHF papers, so the outline front-loads the conceptual building blocks the papers assume: what language models are and how RL works, since neither can be taken for granted. The motivation node ("what problem") gives orientation before mechanics. The middle nodes break RLHF into its two distinct technical pieces—reward modeling vs. policy optimization—which are the parts most likely to confuse a newcomer and which map directly onto the structure of the InstructGPT paper. The "human feedback vs. fixed reward" node captures the core conceptual insight rather than mechanics, keeping it MECE from the two mechanism nodes. The end-to-end pipeline node synthesizes the pieces, mirroring how papers present the three-stage process. A final node explicitly bridges to the papers themselves, matching the stated goal. Excluded: math derivations, coding/tooling, and deep RL theory, per the confirmed understanding prioritizing conceptual orientation over implementation or rigor."
